brief.subject: Fake debt collectors halted, plus pricing and privacy crackdowns
brief.headline: Court Freezes Phantom Debt Collectors; FTC Hits Retail and Rental Price Tricks
brief.dek: A court froze a debt operation accused of posing as lawyers, and regulators pursue shelf-price, rent and health-data cases.
brief.lede: At the FTC's request, a federal court froze a debt collection operation accused of pressuring people to pay debts they often didn't owe. Fake legal threats remain a classic intimidation scam.

sections.heading: Phantom Debt Collectors Frozen
bullets: A federal court temporarily halted the operation and froze its assets after an FTC request.
Collectors allegedly posed as a law firm or claimed ties to attorneys, a tactic meant to scare people into paying.
They allegedly threatened to contact employers and family members, so treat such threats as a red flag.
Many targeted debts were frequently not owed, so verify any debt before paying a cent.

sections.heading: Health Data Shared With Advertisers?
bullets: Five states joined the FTC's lawsuit against telehealth provider Hims and Hers through an amended complaint.
The suit alleges sensitive health information went to third-party ad platforms despite privacy promises.
It also alleges users were misled about billing and cancellation, so check telehealth subscription terms closely.

sections.heading: Register Price Higher Than Shelf Tag
bullets: Family Dollar will pay $63 million to settle claims from the FTC and 17 states.
Shoppers were allegedly charged more at checkout than prices on shelves, tags and ads.
Comparing your receipt to the shelf price is a simple way to catch overcharges.

sections.heading: Hidden Costs in Rent and Car Ads
bullets: Progress Residential and owner Pretium Partners will pay $49.75 million over alleged deceptive rental pricing.
The FTC calls it the largest enforcement matter it has taken against a landlord.
Separately, Long Island dealer Stream Auto Outlet settled claims its advertised prices were far below what buyers paid.

brief.seo_description: Court freezes fake debt collectors posing as lawyers; FTC settles Family Dollar and rental pricing cases; states join Hims and Hers privacy suit.

items.title: Progress Residential and Owner Pretium Partners to Pay $49.75 Million to Settle FTC and States’ Charges Over Deceptive Rental Pricing Practices and Other Unlawful Conduct
